title: Israel Sets October 27, 2026 Election Date; Knesset to Dissolve July 17 — First Full Term Since 1988
detail: On July 12, 2026, Netanyahu's coalition confirmed that Israel's next national election will be held October 27, 2026, with the 25th Knesset set to formally dissolve on July 17. Knesset Legal Adviser Sagit Afik recommended the timeline; Speaker Amir Ohana and Coalition Whip Ofir Katz confirmed it. The October 27 date — described as 'the latest possible date permitted by law' — was chosen because earlier October dates would fall too close to the High Holidays and the October 7 anniversary. Completing the term marks the first time since 1988 that a Knesset has served its full four years, despite the war, the October 7 accountability crisis, and repeated coalition crises over Haredi conscription. The election will be fought substantially over the unresolved question of an independent October 7 state commission of inquiry, with the opposition Beyachad alliance (Bennett-Lapid) pledging a 'day one' commission if it wins.
